metadata.title: SAR - Service-Internal Fine-Grained Authorization (Envoke)
metadata.remarks: Assessment result identifying that fine-grained authorization within the Envoke service is enforced using service-internal roles rather than Entra ID group-based authorization. Coarse-grained access is correctly enforced via Entra ID SSO.

findings.title: Fine-Grained Authorization Enforced Internally by Service
findings.description: The Envoke Email Campaign Platform enforces fine-grained authorization (e.g., Author, Manager, Sender, Administrator) using service-internal roles rather than Entra ID group mappings. Entra ID SSO correctly enforces authentication and coarse-grained access to the service.

associated-risk.title: Role Governance and Attestation Gaps
associated-risk.description: Service-internal role models can make centralized role enumeration, periodic attestation, and timely removal of fine-grained access more cumbersome, increasing the risk of stale or over-privileged roles.

remediations.title: Improve Fine-Grained Authorization Governance
remediations.description: Address governance and attestation limitations introduced by service-internal role enforcement while retaining Entra ID-based coarse-grained access control.

tasks.title: Maintain Central Role Inventory
tasks.description: Document Envoke service roles, role holders, and role assignment criteria in a centrally accessible inventory.

tasks.title: Periodic Role Attestation
tasks.description: Establish a periodic review and attestation process for Envoke service roles to ensure continued appropriateness.

tasks.title: Validate Role Removal on Access Revocation
tasks.description: Confirm that removal of Entra ID access to Envoke results in timely removal of all associated service-internal roles.
